features.title: From scattered setup to maintainable Agent Teams.
features.subtitle: CrewBee focuses on maintainability: Team assets, domain rules, tools / skills strategy, review flows, and completion criteria are kept together instead of scattered across prompts and projects.

cards.title: Engineer Agent Teams for domain-specific workflows
cards.desc: Not just agents: define tools / skills strategy, workflow, shared rules, review flow, and completion criteria. Turn a repeatable way of working into a reusable Team.

cards.title: Simple stays fast. Complex gets support.
cards.desc: CrewBee does not turn multi-agent work into a default ritual. Simple tasks stay single-agent and fast; complex tasks add support agents, review, validation, and completion criteria.

cards.title: The Leader owns the decision context
cards.desc: The Leader keeps user goals, project constraints, support findings, review feedback, validation results, and risks together for final judgment and delivery.

cards.title: Context-isolated delegation

paragraphs: AI can generate code quickly, but reliable delivery still needs requirement understanding, codebase exploration, design judgment, implementation, independent review, validation, and final delivery.

When these concerns are scattered across prompts, agents, rules, and ad-hoc conventions, agent workflows become difficult to maintain. CrewBee turns these ways of working into maintainable Agent Team assets.
why.emphasis: CrewBee’s value is reusable Team assets for responsibilities, rules, review flows, and completion criteria.

before: Completion criteria are hard to reuse
after: Reusable review flow and completion criteria
Simple tasks stay light; complex tasks get support

how.title: How CrewBee works
how.subtitle: Define Teams as assets, connect them to OpenCode, choose a Leader or Executor, and run the workflow that matches the task.

steps.desc: Define the Team mission, Leader, members, shared policy, workflow, tools / skills strategy, review path, and completion criteria.
Start with OpenCode today. CrewBee makes Team assets selectable and runnable as agent workflows in OpenCode.
Pick Leader for complex tasks that need ownership, delegation, review, validation, and final delivery. Pick Executor for clear, local, low-risk tasks.
Simple tasks use the lightweight path; complex tasks add codebase exploration, focused implementation, independent review, validation, and delivery notes.

modes.label: Leader
modes.desc: Owns requirement understanding, task thread, support delegation, review synthesis, final judgment, and delivery.

modes.label: Executor
modes.desc: Best for clear, local implementation, fixes, and debugging. It does not own the complex task thread.

team.title: Team packages are engineering assets. Copy, modify, and contribute them.
paragraphs: A CrewBee Team is not a prompt file. It is a structured Team package with mission, Leader, members, shared policy, workflow, tools / skills strategy, review criteria, completion criteria, and human-readable documentation.
Start with the built-in Coding Team. Copy a template. Adjust roles, shared policy, tools / skills strategy, review flow, and completion criteria. Turn your own way of working into a reusable Team.

opencode.title: OpenCode-ready today

inspired.title: Inspired by the open-source Agent ecosystem.
paragraphs: CrewBee is inspired by community projects such as OpenCode and oh-my-openagent. These projects make the value of Agent Team workflows in real development environments clearer.
CrewBee continues in this direction by organizing Agent Teams into manageable, projectable, configurable, and reusable engineering assets.

items.a: No. CrewBee uses prompts, but its core is Team definitions, Agent profiles, session binding, delegation tooling, review flows, and completion criteria. It turns agent workflows into maintainable, runnable Team assets.

items.q: Is CrewBee a flat agent list?
items.a: No. CrewBee is not just more roles. It emphasizes Teams, Leaders, members, shared policy, workflow, review flow, and completion criteria.

No. CrewBee is designed as a Team definition and projection layer for agent harnesses. OpenCode is the first supported host because it provides a practical plugin path today. The long-term direction is to keep Team definitions portable and adapt them to more agent harnesses over time.

items.q: Does CrewBee make every task multi-agent?
items.a: No. CrewBee does not turn multi-agent work into a default ritual. Simple tasks stay lightweight; complex tasks add codebase exploration, focused implementation, independent review, validation, and delivery.

items.q: Why does the main agent / Leader matter?
items.a: In complex work, support agents only see part of the picture. CrewBee keeps goals, constraints, support findings, review feedback, verification results, and risks together in the main agent’s decision context.

Support agents do code exploration, research, review, or multimodal reading in dedicated contexts, then return high-signal findings to the main agent. This reduces main-agent context pollution and attention load.

items.q: Where does CrewBee sit in the OpenCode ecosystem?
items.a: CrewBee uses OpenCode as the current adapter, not as its whole identity. It is a Team definition and projection layer that organizes prompts, agents, rules, review flows, and completion criteria into maintainable Team assets that can later be adapted to more agent harnesses.

items.q: Is Project Context fully implemented today?
items.a: No. Project Context is a Roadmap / Next-stage direction. The goal is to help long-running project agents avoid onboarding from zero every session, not to claim a mature current capability.
CrewBee starts with OpenCode today. More Agent Harness adapters belong to the Roadmap.

Yes. CrewBee’s core is Team definition and projection, so you can create ResearchOpsTeam, DocumentationTeam, MarketingOpsTeam, ReleaseOpsTeam, and more. The flagship public example today is the built-in Coding Team.
The easiest contribution is not changing the core runtime. Contribute Team templates, docs, use cases, installation feedback, FAQ improvements, or show your Team in Discussions.
